solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Mrs with pride's shown off during traditional bustle

indicators.note: showing off is putting on a display, so these letters are paraded about in a new order

parts.note: taken as written, the apostrophe ignored
over means during, as in 'over the weekend'

explanation.surface: A proud woman makes a show of herself amid the bustle of a traditional occasion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bustle' looks like activity, but it is the padded frame once worn under a skirt.
explanation.definitionFit: A dress improver was the Victorian name for the padded frame worn at the back of a skirt, also called a bustle.

clue.text: US attorney limits mischief displaying righteousness

indicators.note: to limit something is to set bounds on either side of it, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: District Attorney, the US public prosecutor
mischief in the sense of injury or damage

explanation.surface: An American prosecutor curbs wrongdoing and so shows himself upright.
explanation.definitionFit: Dharma in Hindu and Buddhist thought is moral law and right conduct, hence righteousness.

clue.text: Speech but not on outlying legal principle?

indicators.note: the two letters spelling 'on' are dropped, taken from the far ends of the word rather than together

explanation.surface: A lawyer's address strays from the point of legal principle.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the first O and last N of ORATION, which together spell ON, to leave RATIO.
explanation.definitionFit: In law the ratio decidendi, often just 'ratio', is the principle on which a court's decision rests.

clue.text: Mining area in Cornwall and in Dorset (tin)

indicators.note: the second 'in' says the word sits inside the following run of letters

parts.note: the letters straddle the county name and the bracketed word

explanation.surface: A note on tin mining in the south-west counties of Cornwall and Dorset.
explanation.definitionFit: In Cornish mining a sett is the tract of ground leased for working minerals.

clue.text: Sea quarry regularly culled?

indicators.note: culling at regular intervals removes every other letter, keeping the rest

parts.note: first, third, fifth, seventh and ninth letters

explanation.surface: Fish caught at sea are thinned out at intervals by fishermen.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: the saury is a sea fish that is regularly caught, the question mark flagging the double duty.
explanation.definitionFit: The saury is a slender marine fish, prey commonly netted by fishing fleets, so a sea quarry often culled.

clue.text: Cash low — get a load of that!

parts.note: to low is to make a cow's sound
la is an old exclamation of surprise

explanation.surface: Someone short of money exclaims at what they see.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Low' looks like 'short of', but here it is the verb a cow does.
explanation.definitionFit: Moola is slang for money.

clue.text: Furry garment? Pile's wasted on bits of sham ermine

indicators.note: something wasted is ruined, so the letters are knocked out of shape and rearranged
only small parts of the following words are used, here their opening letters

explanation.surface: The nap of an imitation fur has worn away on a fake ermine coat.
explanation.definitionFit: A pelisse is a long cloak or coat, traditionally lined or trimmed with fur.

clue.text: Wherein vermin perish wretchedly, trap sprung over it

indicators.note: a sprung trap has snapped apart, so its letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Pests die miserably in a snapped trap.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'over' puts the first piece above the second.
explanation.definitionFit: A rat pit was an enclosure where dogs were set to kill rats for sport and wagers.

clue.text: Wrist protector, advantage when covering tense support

parts.note: van is the short form of advantage in tennis scoring

explanation.surface: A wrist guard gives an edge when it covers a taut support strap.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue VAN 'covering' T simply sits above it.
explanation.definitionFit: A vantbrace was the piece of armour guarding the forearm, from the wrist up.

clue.text: Pet cups like this may have been mixed for the party

indicators.note: mixing implies the letters were stirred together into another order

parts.note: these letters are what the answer lacks; mixed with it they would make the phrase

explanation.surface: Favourite drinking vessels were probably shaken up for the celebration.
explanation.walkthrough: A composite: PET plus the answer mixed together gives THE PARTY, so take PET out of THE PARTY and rearrange the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhyta, plural of rhyton, are ancient Greek drinking horns, often shaped as an animal's head.

clue.text: Husband greeting past, being up for it

explanation.surface: A husband says hello to bygone days, keen as ever.
explanation.walkthrough: Used adjectivally, as in a 'have-a-go hero', it means willing to tackle something.
explanation.definitionFit: A have-a-go type is game, willing to try or intervene, which is what being up for it means.

clue.text: Create embarrassment in adult party

parts.note: standard abbreviation, as in film ratings

explanation.surface: Causing a scene at a grown-up celebration.
explanation.definitionFit: To abash is to make someone feel ashamed or disconcerted.

clue.text: Turf-cutters' tool — special course required

parts.note: a lane is a course, as in a running track

explanation.surface: Peat diggers need a particular route for their implement.
explanation.definitionFit: A slane is an Irish spade with a side wing used for cutting peat turves.

clue.text: Top men, too busy, I'll never inflect

indicators.note: busy things are in a bustle of motion, so the letters are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: A busy executive declares they will never change their tone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inflect' looks like modulating the voice; in grammar it means changing a word's ending.
explanation.definitionFit: A monoptote is a noun with only one case form, so it never changes its ending.

clue.text: Little Mary receives a number in flowing fashion?

indicators.note: one who receives takes something in, so the name holds the number

parts.note: a pet form of the name Mary
any number will do; this one fits

explanation.surface: A small girl called Mary is given a number for her flowing dance.
explanation.definitionFit: Molten means melted and flowing, so moltenly describes acting in a fluid, liquid manner.

clue.text: Ferdinand maybe on trial for unruly behaviour

parts.note: a try is a trial or attempt; 'on' places the footballer first

explanation.surface: A footballer is in the dock over his rowdy conduct.
explanation.walkthrough: Rio Ferdinand is a former England football captain; 'Ferdinand' tempts toward the Spanish king or Shakespeare's prince.
explanation.definitionFit: Riotry is an old word for riotous conduct, the noisy disorder of a riot.

clue.text: An artist orders this facsimile in RA

indicators.note: the phrase is put in order, that is arranged from other letters

parts.note: these letters, with the next, are what the phrase has besides the answer

explanation.surface: A painter commissions a copy of a work at the Royal Academy.
explanation.walkthrough: A composite: the answer plus IN and RA rearranged makes AN ARTIST, so remove those letters from AN ARTIST and rearrange the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Stat is short for photostat, a photographic copy of a document.

clue.text: I'm surprised about Globe Theatre — it's often full

indicators.note: about means around, so the exclamation goes round the other pieces

parts.note: my! is an exclamation of surprise
a globe is round, the shape of the letter

explanation.surface: Someone is astonished that Shakespeare's Globe is usually packed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Globe Theatre' reads as Shakespeare's playhouse but splits into two separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase 'the full monty' means the whole lot, so the word is very often found with full.

clue.text: Taste of soup in ladle requiring herb

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: to bail is to scoop out water, as one ladles

indicators.note: a taste is only a little, so just the opening letter of the word is used

explanation.surface: A cook samples soup from the ladle and decides it needs a herb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ladle' is a verb here, synonymous with bail (scoop out).
explanation.definitionFit: Basil is a common culinary herb.

clue.text: Humbly loading funeral vehicle, being less calm …

indicators.note: loading something puts a cargo inside it

parts.note: low as an adverb means humbly, as in bow low

explanation.surface: Mourners meekly load a hearse on a gusty day.
explanation.definitionFit: Blowier is the comparative of blowy, windy, so the weather is less still.

clue.text: Off-licence in Perth, say, preserves rent (11, two words)

parts.note: to bottle fruit is to preserve it
past tense of tear, as rent is of rend

explanation.surface: A shop in Perth keeps the rent money safe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rent' looks like money paid for a property; it is the past tense of rend, tore. An off-licence is a British shop selling alcohol to take away.
explanation.definitionFit: Bottle store is the Australian and South African term for a shop selling liquor to take away.

clue.text: … As a result of this, nuisance about funeral's end?

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece goes round the other

parts.note: a bore is a tiresome nuisance

indicators.note: the end of the word means its final letter alone is used

explanation.surface: Following from the previous clue, a pest is causing trouble at the close of a funeral.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links to 18 down: the definition means the thing that makes the weather less calm.
explanation.definitionFit: A blore is a strong blast of wind, the cause of it being blowier.

clue.text: Relax in centre of settee — part of family crockery produced (6, two words)

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other
only the middle of the following word is used

explanation.surface: Lounging on the sofa while the best china comes out.
explanation.definitionFit: A tea set is a matching set of cups, saucers and pot, part of a household's crockery.

clue.text: In leaving chaotic terminus, it's not worth betting on

indicators.note: chaos is disorder, so the remaining letters fall into another order
the word named first departs from the longer one

explanation.surface: Leaving a crowded station, a punter decides a horse is a poor bet.
explanation.definitionFit: Stumer is slang for a dud, including a racehorse certain to lose.

clue.text: A drop of rum in the pud? Delay no longer!

definitions.note: an obsolete word, which the 'no longer' signals

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: pud is a child's word for a hand or paw

indicators.note: a drop is a tiny amount, so only the first letter is used

explanation.surface: A cook splashes rum into the Christmas pudding and urges everyone to start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pud' looks like pudding but is an old word for a hand; 'no longer' marks the word as obsolete.
explanation.definitionFit: Frist is an obsolete verb meaning to postpone or grant time, so a delay in older English.

clue.text: Fish brought back just after being caught: bit of income for W. African

definitions.text: bit of income for W. African

indicators.note: the second piece is caught inside the first
bringing something back returns it the way it came, so read it backwards

parts.note: on can mean immediately after, as in 'on arrival'

explanation.surface: A fish is landed just after it was hooked, earning an African fisherman a little money.
explanation.definitionFit: The leone is the currency of Sierra Leone, so a unit of a West African's income.

clue.text: Cause of financial crash pa ignored before he gets commercial opportunity

indicators.note: letters that are ignored are left out of the word

parts.note: a panic on the markets brings a crash

explanation.surface: Dad, unaware of what caused the crash, still finds a business opening.
explanation.definitionFit: A niche is a specialised gap in the market that a business can exploit.

clue.text: Part of flowering plant most support with bit of twine

indicators.note: most of a word is all of it but the last letter
a bit is a small piece, here the first letter

explanation.surface: A gardener props up most of a plant, tying it with a little string.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Most support' tempts toward BRA alone, but it is a shortened BRACE.
explanation.definitionFit: A bract is a modified leaf at the base of a flower or flower stalk.

clue.text: British Raj done for, independence produces staple food grain

indicators.note: something done for is wrecked, so the letters are broken up and rearranged

parts.note: abbreviation, as in a political label

explanation.surface: With British rule over in India, independence brings a basic cereal crop.
explanation.definitionFit: Bajri is the Indian name for pearl millet, a staple grain.

clue.text: Head of candle hot? Fair enough — snuff it

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

parts.note: standard abbreviation, as on a tap
oke is a variant of OK, meaning all right

explanation.surface: A candle flame is too hot, so someone agrees to put it out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Snuff it' looks like putting out a candle; it is slang for dying.
explanation.definitionFit: To choke can mean to die, and to snuff it is slang for dying.

clue.text: God seen as inspiring part of scripture for canon

indicators.note: to inspire is literally to breathe in, so the god takes the other piece inside

explanation.surface: A deity is said to have inspired the Bible text that a churchman reads.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Canon' looks like a clergyman; here it is a list or roll.
explanation.definitionFit: A canon can be a list or catalogue, and a rota is a list of duties or names in turn.

clue.text: E. Asian language inscription in Norman church

indicators.note: something inscribed in is written within, so the word sits inside the following letters

parts.note: spans the end of one word and the start of the next

explanation.surface: A carving in an oriental script is found in an old Norman church.
explanation.definitionFit: Manchu is the Tungusic language of the Manchu people of north-east China.

clue.text: Would they survive 1 October? Not if deadly shots start off thus

indicators.note: where each word starts is its opening letter, and these are taken

parts.note: first letters of the four words

explanation.surface: Will the birds live past the opening of the shooting season? Not if the guns are accurate.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain pheasant shooting opens on 1 October.
explanation.definitionFit: A nid or nide is a brood of pheasants, the young birds shot in the season.

clue.text: Worry about damaged icons with corrosion of metal parts

indicators.note: about means around, so the worry encloses the other piece

parts.note: to irk is to annoy or worry

indicators.note: damaged things are knocked out of shape, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Fretting over religious images ruined by rusting fittings.
explanation.definitionFit: Ironsick describes a wooden ship whose iron bolts and nails have rusted, loosening the timbers.

clue.text: Teasel may show fifty such

indicators.note: a thing that may show something can reveal it in a new arrangement

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty; this letter is removed

explanation.surface: A spiky teasel head might bear fifty bristles.
explanation.walkthrough: A composite: the answer plus L rearranged spells TEASEL, while the whole clue also describes the plant's bristly head.
explanation.definitionFit: Setae are bristles, and a teasel's flower head is covered in stiff bristly points.

clue.text: Fish holding rod wrongly? Critics may differ about it

indicators.note: the fish holds the other piece inside it
done wrongly, the letters come out in the wrong order

explanation.surface: An angler holds his rod clumsily while onlookers argue about it.
explanation.definitionFit: Hardoke is a plant named in King Lear whose identity scholars dispute, burdock and charlock among the guesses.

clue.text: Olga, Maria or Irina, head of operator's back-up team? (13, two words)

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a sister on stage, from Chekhov's play Three Sisters
second meaning: the senior nurse assisting a surgeon in the operating theatre

explanation.walkthrough: Olga, Maria (Masha) and Irina are Chekhov's Three Sisters, so each is a sister of the theatre. In Britain a sister is a senior nurse.
explanation.definitionFit: A theatre sister is the senior nurse in charge of an operating theatre, supporting the surgeon.
